JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- from the respondent, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in road traffic accident.
2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:

On 21-10-2022 at about 4.45 a.m., near Amar Tower, opposite to Sanman Hotel,
Bengaluru, the petitioner was going to BMTC bus-stand from T.B. Tower by walk.

At that time, all of a sudden a KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F- 1328 came from Upparpete Police Station towards Majestic bus station, driven by its driver with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and front left side wheel of the said bus ran over his left leg and he has sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as labor and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Upparpete Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said bus for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.1 has appeared through his counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

He has contended that, at the time of accident the bus bearing No.KA-40-F-1328 was proceeding from Bengaluru to Chintamani and when it reached T.B. road, Amar Junction, Bengaluru infront of Sanman Hotel, around 4.45 a.m., at that time the petitioner clearly in an inebriated state, staggered down the road, struggling to keep his balance with unsteady step and fell in front of the right side of the bus.

Seeing the same, the driver of the KSRTC bus in question applied breaks and steered the bus towards his extreme left to avoid run over the petitioner, in which the petitioner sustained minor injuries.
The negligent and irresponsible act of the petitioner in a busy road at night is the proximate cause for the accident.

The careless and negligent act of the petitioner was the main cause for the accident and the respondent or its driver is not responsible in any way or manner for any of the claims in the petitioner and the same is liable to be dismissed against this respondent.

He has Kariyappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111196269/
2 denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.

Further it is contended that, the police investigation officer without conducting proper investigation, without observing vehicle position and nature of damages and without applying mind, simply colluding with petitioner with sole intention to make a wrongful gain from the respondents.

Hence, falsely implicating the driver of this respondent, this is opposed to the facts,
probability and circumstances of the case.
Hence, the petition is liable to be dismissed against this respondent.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident, alleged to have occurred on 21-10-2022 at about 4.45 a.m., near T.B.
road, Amar Junction, in front of Sanman Hotel, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC Bus, bearing registration No. KA-40-F- 1328 ?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.

What order or Award ?
6.
In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 13 documents as Ex.P.1 to 13.

On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has got examined its driver, who is respondent No.2 in the case, as R.W.1 and got marked 2 documents as Ex.R.1 and 2.
7.
I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 21-10-2022 at about 4:45 a.m., when he was crossing the road by walk, from T.B. Tower towards BMTC bus-stand, near Amar Tower, opposite to Sanman Hotel, all of a sudden the offending KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F- 1328 came from Upparpete Police Station towards Majestic bus-station, with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to him.
Due to the said impact, he fell down on the road and front left side wheel of the said bus ran over his left leg and he has sustained grievous injuries.

Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident he was working as labor and was earning a sum of Kariyappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111196269/
3 Rs.25,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 13 documents as Ex.P.1 to 13.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.4 is true copy of sketch, Ex.P.5 is true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.6 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.7 is OPD book, Ex.P.8 is OPD slip,
Ex.P.9 and 10 are discharge summaries, Ex.P.11 are prescriptions, Ex.P.12 are medical bills and Ex.P.13 is notarized copy of Aadhar card of petitioner.
11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 6, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F-1328 and dashing the same to the petitioner, who was pedestrian and crossing the road.
Further it reveals that, due to said impact, the petitioner has fell down and front left side wheel of the said bus has moved on his left leg and he has sustained grievous injuries.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge- sheet, marked as Ex.P.3, has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA- 40-F-1328.
12.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, there is no dispute with regard date, time and place of accident, involvement of offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA- 40-F-1328 in the alleged accident.

But, the respondent No.1 has denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and has taken specific defence that, the said accident has taken place solely due to negligence and irresponsible act of the petitioner in a busy road and in the night hours and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of said bus.
Further it is contended that, the petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional Police has lodged a false case against the driver of KSRTC bus in question.
But, the respondent has failed to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of R.W.1, who is the none other than the accused/driver of offending vehicle, there is no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that,
the said accident has taken place due to the sole negligence of the petitioner himself and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F-1328.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F- 1328 and dashing the same to the petitioner, who was pedestrian and crossing the road.
Further it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries to his left leg in the aid accident.

Though the learned counsel for respondent has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which establishes that, he has sustained injuries due to his self negligence or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

13. The Ex.P.4 sketch and Ex.P.5 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place in the middle of T.B. road, Amar Junction, infront of Sanman Hotel, Bengaluru, due to Kariyappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111196269/
4 dashing of offending KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F-1328 to the petitioner, who was pedestrian on the said road.
Further, it is not the case of the respondent that, the accident is caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending KSRTC bus.

Further, the investigation officer has clearly stated in his Ex.P.3 final report/charge-sheet that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No. KA- 40-F-1328.
Admittedly the said charge-sheet has not been challenged by the driver or owner of the offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-40-F-1328.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending KSRTC bus in the accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.6 wound certificate, Ex.P.7 OPD book, Ex.P.8 OPD slip and Ex.P.9 and 10 discharge summaries, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
As per the said documents, the petitioner has suffered closed IT fracture of right femur and open type 3B fracture of medial maloli of left side.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.1 to show that, the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-40-F-1328 and the injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

17. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 21-10-2022 at about 4.45 a.m., near T.B. road, Amar Junction, in front of Sanman Hotel, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-40-F-1328.

Hence, I answer Issue Kariyappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111196269/
5 No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2: While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-40-F-1328 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained closed IT fracture of right femur and open type 3B fracture of medial maloli of left side and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport,
actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
19. Towards loss of future income:
The petitioner has deposed that, earlier to the accident, he was working as labor and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.

Due to the accidental injuries,
he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
But, the petitioner has neither produced any document nor examined the doctor to establish that, due to injuries sustained in the accident he has suffered any physical disability or deformity.

The petitioner has failed to prove that, due to accidental injuries he has suffered any physical disability and he is not in a position to continue his avocation or perform his regular work and thereby, he has lost his earning capacity.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation under head loss of future income due to permanent physical disability does not arise at all.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
20. Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.6,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 17 medical bills, as per Ex.P.12.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.8,010/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,010/- under the head of medical expenses.
21. Pain and sufferings:
In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e. closed IT fracture of right femur and open type 3B fracture of medial maloli of left side.

As per Ex.P.9 and 10 discharge summaries, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 37 days from 21-10-2022 to 09-11-2022 and 17-12-2022 to 02-01-2023 in Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru and ESIC Medical College, PGIMSR and Model Hospital, Bengaluru.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into consideration the injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.60,000/-
is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
22. Attendant charges:

As per Ex.P.9 and 10 discharge summaries, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 37 days in Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru and ESIC Medical College,
PGIMSR and Model Hospital, Bengaluru.

He might have spent considerable amount towards Kariyappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111196269/
6 attendant charges during the said period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 37 = Rs.37,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
23. Food and nourishment:

As per Ex.P.9 and 10 discharge summaries, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 37 days in Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru and ESIC Medical College,
PGIMSR and Model Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during the said period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 37 = Rs.29,600/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
24. Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Chowdeshwari Nagara, Laggere,
Bengaluru, the accident has occurred near T.B. road, Amar Junction, in front of Sanman Hotel,
Bengaluru and he has taken treatment at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru and ESIC Medical College,
PGIMSR and Model Hospital, Bengaluru.

entities.text:
ESIC Medical College,
PGIMSR and Model Hospital, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places, compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
25. Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as a labor and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do work and continue his avocation.
But, he has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was working as a labor and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2022.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month.

The petitioner has taken treatment for 37 days as in-patient at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru and ESIC Medical College,
PGIMSR and Model Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries caused to him.
He might have taken rest for about 4 months and lost his income for the said period.

Therefore, Rs.15,500 x 4 =
Rs.62,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
26. Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 65 years and unfortunately he has suffered grievous injuries in the said accident and undergone treatment for 37 days as in-patient in Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru and ESIC Medical College, PGIMSR and Model Hospital, Bengaluru.

entities.text: ESIC Medical College, PGIMSR and Model Hospital, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further, he might have taken rest for about two months.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities during the said period would be just and reasonable.
27. Future medical expenses:
The petitioner has neither adduced any evidence nor produced any document to show that he requires to undergo any further treatment for the injuries sustained in the accident.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation towards future medical expenses does not arise at all.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.

28. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Loss of future income -Nil- Kariyappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111196269/
7 2.
Medical expenses 8,010-00 3. Pain and sufferings 60,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 37,000-00 5.
Food and nourishment 29,600-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 10,000-00 7. Loss of income during 62,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 30,000-00
9. Future medical expenses -Nil-
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,36,610/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
29. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the driver of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent No.2/driver of offending KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No. KA-40-F-1328 the accident has occurred and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of offending vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the usage of said vehicle.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that,
the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,36,610/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.1, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
30. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.2,36,610/- (Rupees two lakh thirty six thousand six hundred and ten only), with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.

, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained closed IT fracture of right femur and open type 3B fracture of medial maloli of left side and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities during the said period would be just and reasonable.
The petitioner has neither adduced any evidence nor produced any document to show that he requires to undergo any further treatment for the injuries sustained in the accident.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation towards future medical expenses does not arise at all.
